targetedChallenges.challenge: The revise_plan case rests on treating plan.md:L1-L3 as the complete and only artifact, but every cited evidence item is a plan_line observation about what the three lines say — none of them demonstrates that no external spec, appendix, or runbook exists. The 'plan is unexecutable' conclusion is therefore load-bearing on an unproven negative: if a linked spec already fixes the validation contract, flag config, and rollback thresholds, the underspecification findings collapse and accept_plan becomes viable.

The 'missing observability' risk (ev_..._bbbb_4) infers that no metrics/monitoring capability exists from the mere absence of a monitoring step in plan.md. A three-line plan naming only deltas can legitimately assume pre-existing error-rate telemetry; absence in the plan text is not evidence of absence in the system, so this risk is weaker than stated and should not on its own force revision.

assumptionReviews.rationale: The assumption's own how_to_verify requires confirming plan.md has no additional sections or external links. The cited evidence (ev_..._aaaa_1..3) only characterizes the content of L1-L3; nothing in the frozen context establishes the presence or absence of a linked appendix, so the claim of completeness cannot be confirmed from supplied ids.

Verifying this assumption requires confirming no linked spec/runbook accompanies plan.md. All four cited evidence items are plan_line observations of what L1-L3 omit; none checks for or rules out an external appendix. The absence of detail within the lines does not prove the three lines are the entire plan, so the load-bearing completeness claim remains unverified.
